title: Sequential-test probe adjudication (SPRT), margin-gated mismatch, corrected horizon (H26-6 halves)
question: Does the SPRT hold both H26-6 halves: no conviction of the honest, conviction of the 99.5%-agreeing substitute within the registered budget?
m305a_note: run 1 VOIDED on its own H2 bound: the registered (8000, 0.95) budget/bound pair was consistent with the instrument (calibration power 0.9552 at 8000), but run-1's H2 run count (300) under-resolved the measurement (+/-1.3%). M305a step 1 calibrated the power from the registered rates (never fitted to the failed verdict); step 2 re-runs the verdict at h2_runs=5000, budget and bounds unchanged. Run-1 evidence stays on record as evidence_void_h2.json.

registered_notes.honest_rate: p0 = 0.002 per probed session: the registered honest rate for margin-gated divergent hardware
registered_notes.substitute: p1 = 0.005: the 99.5%-agreeing substitute of finding A5
registered_notes.horizon_context: the wall-clock horizon median/rho is recorded per probe rate against 1/(rho*delta) as context, not gated - the SPRT trades first-evidence speed for a registered false-conviction rate

interpretation_registered_before_running.h1_fails: the honest contributor IS convicted - the sequential test's false-conviction rate exceeds its registered bound; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.h2_fails: the substitute escapes conviction - the sequential test cannot see a 0.5% deviation at this budget; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.both_hold: H26-6 PASS: margin-gated probes do not convict the honest, and the sequential test convicts the substitute
